name: Spain
summary: Spain taxes residents' capital gains and dividends at up to 30% and levies an annual wealth tax plus a solidarity tax on fortunes above EUR 3m. Inheritance and gift tax is paid by the heir; the regions control it, and most rebate 99-100% for children, while Catalonia, Asturias, Aragón, Galicia and Navarra tax large inheritances heavily. Region of residence decides much of the outcome (see subnational file). Newcomers taking a Spanish job or directorship can use the 6-year Beckham regime, which exempts foreign investment income.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence (state rules)
regimes.description: Resident individual taxed on worldwide income and wealth; state rules shown (regional variations in the subnational file).
regimes.eligibility: Tax residence: more than 183 days in Spain in the calendar year, or main centre of economic interests in Spain; presumption if spouse and minor children live in Spain.

capital_gains.summary: Capital gains of a resident individual go to the savings base (base del ahorro) and are taxed at 19% to 30%; the top 30% applies to savings income above EUR 300,000 (since 2025). The scale is the same in every common-regime region because the regions cannot change the savings scale.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Savings scale (state + regional half combined, arts. 66 and 76 LIRPF): 19% to EUR 6,000; 21% to 50,000; 23% to 200,000; 27% to 300,000; 30% above. Losses offset savings income within limits; 4-year carry-forward. Gains on the sale of the main home are exempt if reinvested in a new main home or for sellers aged 65+.
capital_gains.regional_differences: No regional difference in the common regime. Navarra and the Basque Country have their own IRPF with a different savings scale (top 28% in Navarra and Bizkaia, see the subnational file).
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Exit tax (art. 95 bis LIRPF): a resident for at least 10 of the last 15 years who leaves Spain is taxed on the unrealised gain on shares if their market value exceeds EUR 4m, or EUR 1m with a stake above 25%; deferral is available on moves within the EU/EEA. Funds (IIC) can be switched without tax (traspasos). Selling Spanish property also triggers the municipal IIVTNU.

capital_gains.rate_basis: Top marginal rate of the combined savings scale (30% above EUR 300,000) for a large gain; no holding period matters. Real estate gains of individuals are savings income too (municipal IIVTNU on Spanish land comes on top and is not included).
capital_gains.professional_trader: Gains on securities remain savings income for a private investor regardless of volume; only an organised business activity (e.g. a dealer with staff and premises) would move income to the general base (state+regional up to about 45-54%).
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: None. Short- and long-term gains are taxed alike; 2-month/1-year wash-sale rules defer losses on repurchased securities.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Residents are taxed on worldwide gains with a credit for foreign tax (art. 80 LIRPF). Foreign assets above EUR 50,000 per category must be reported on Modelo 720.

dividends.summary: Dividends are savings income taxed at 19% to 30% (30% above EUR 300,000 of savings income), domestic and foreign alike. Foreign withholding tax is credited up to the Spanish tax on that income.
dividends.exemptions_thresholds: No dividend exemption for individuals (the former EUR 1,500 exemption was abolished in 2015).
dividends.regional_differences: None in the common regime; Navarra and the Basque Country have their own scales (see subnational file).

dividends.rate_basis: Top marginal rate of the savings scale (art. 66/76 LIRPF) for a large portfolio; credit for foreign WHT limited to the treaty rate and to the Spanish tax on that income (art. 80 LIRPF).
dividends.withholding_outbound: 19% domestic WHT on dividends to non-residents; 0% to qualifying EU parents (5% for 1 year); treaty rates usually 0-15%.
dividends.treaty_network: About 90-plus treaties in force (PwC lists 92 entries), including the US (15% portfolio dividends) and all EU states.
dividends.holding_company_notes: Spanish companies get a 95% participation exemption on qualifying dividends and gains (stakes of at least 5% held 1 year); see corporate. No holding structure is scored for Spain: a company holding a diversified listed portfolio pays 25% on portfolio gains and dividends (the 95% exemption of art. 21 LIS needs a stake of at least 5% held one year), an asset-holding company (entidad patrimonial) cannot use the reduced SME rates and its shares get no wealth-tax business exemption, and distributions are taxed again at up to 30%, so with EUR 400,000 a year withdrawn it costs more than personal holding; a SICAV's 1% rate is out of reach for a single family since the 2022 minimum-shareholder rules.

wealth_tax.summary: Spain levies an annual wealth tax (Impuesto sobre el Patrimonio, IP) on residents' worldwide net wealth at 0.2% to 3.5% above a EUR 700,000 allowance (state rules), plus a state 'solidarity' tax on large fortunes (ITSGF) above EUR 3m that only bites where the regional IP is lower. The regions set allowances, scales and rebates, so the real burden depends on the region (see subnational file). This national entry uses the state rules, which apply as such in Castilla-La Mancha, Castilla y León, Ceuta and Melilla.
wealth_tax.exemptions_thresholds: State allowance EUR 700,000 per person (art. 28 LIP); main home exempt up to EUR 300,000 (art. 4.Nueve); qualifying family-business shares exempt (art. 4.Ocho). Joint limit (art. 31 LIP): IRPF + IP may not exceed 60% of the IRPF base (long-term gains excluded), but IP can be cut by at most 80%, so at least 20% of the IP is always payable. A spouse is taxed separately with their own allowance.
wealth_tax.regional_differences: Allowance, scale and rebates vary: e.g. Madrid, Andalucía, La Rioja, Murcia, Cantabria and Extremadura rebate IP but the ITSGF then applies above EUR 3.7m; Galicia rebates 50%; Comunitat Valenciana (EUR 2m allowance from 11 Aug 2026) and Illes Balears (EUR 3m) have high allowances; Navarra and the Basque Country have their own foral wealth taxes.
wealth_tax.important_exceptions: ITSGF (art. 3 Ley 38/2022): 0% on the first EUR 3m of base above a EUR 700,000 allowance, then 1.7%, 2.1% and 3.5% above EUR 10.7m; regional IP actually paid is credited. Created for 2022-2023, extended indefinitely by RDL 8/2023 'until the review of wealth taxation in the regional financing reform'. Under the state scale the IP always exceeds the ITSGF, so the ITSGF adds nothing here.

components.name: Impuesto sobre el Patrimonio, state scale (ITSGF never exceeds it under the state scale)
components.notes: Base is net wealth after the EUR 300,000 main-home exemption. Joint IRPF limit can reduce the tax by up to 80% for low-yield portfolios.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Municipal real estate tax (IBI, roughly 0.4-1.1% of cadastral value) and the municipal land-value gain tax on sales (IIVTNU) are ordinary local taxes and are not modelled as wealth tax.

inheritance.summary: Spain taxes the heir or donee (Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones). Under the state rules a child aged 21+ gets a EUR 15,956.87 allowance and pays 7.65% to 34% (34% above EUR 797,555), so a EUR 10m inheritance costs about 33%. In practice the regional rules apply and most regions rebate 99-100% for children (see subnational file). The state scale itself is used (with regional reductions or rebates) in Aragón, Canarias, Castilla-La Mancha, Castilla y León, Extremadura, La Rioja, Ceuta and Melilla.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: Group II (descendants 21+, spouse, ascendants) reduction EUR 15,956.87 (art. 20.2.a); multiplier 1.0 to 1.2 depending on the heir's own pre-existing wealth (1.2 above EUR 4,020,770.98), so the top effective marginal rate can reach 40.8%.
inheritance.regional_differences: Regions set reductions, scale, multipliers and rebates; the region is the one where the deceased spent most days in the last 5 years (art. 28 Ley 22/2009).
inheritance.important_exceptions: Life insurance proceeds are added to the heir's share; gifts within 3 years accumulate. The brackets assume a heir with pre-existing wealth under EUR 402,678 (multiplier 1.0).

inheritance.gift_tax: Gifts are taxed under the same scale and multipliers but without the parent-child reduction (state rules); most regions grant a 99-100% rebate for gifts to children if made in a notarial deed with the origin of funds stated.
inheritance.business_relief: 95% reduction for qualifying family businesses and shares exempt from wealth tax (art. 20.2.c and 20.6), 10-year holding; regions often raise it to 99%.
inheritance.foreign_assets: Resident heirs/donees are taxed on worldwide acquisitions (personal obligation) with a credit for foreign inheritance tax (art. 23).
inheritance.domicile_rules: Liability follows the heir's residence, not the deceased's: Spanish-resident heirs pay on everything they receive; non-resident heirs pay only on Spanish-situs assets and may apply the regional rules where the deceased resided (DA 2ª, after CJEU C-127/12). No tail after leaving Spain.

regimes.name: Special regime for inbound workers (art. 93 LIRPF, 'Beckham law')
regimes.description: For 6 tax years (year of arrival + 5) the person is taxed like a non-resident: foreign-source dividends, interest and capital gains are not taxed; Spanish-source savings income is taxed at 19-30%; employment income at 24% up to EUR 600,000 and 47% above. Wealth tax only on Spanish assets.
regimes.eligibility: Not Spanish tax resident in the previous 5 years, and moving because of: a Spanish employment contract (including remote work for a foreign employer with the international telework visa), becoming director of a company (if it is a holding/patrimonial company, without a stake of 25% or more), a certified entrepreneurial activity, or highly qualified work for start-ups/R&D. No Spanish permanent establishment. Election within 6 months of starting work. Spouse and children under 25 can join if their combined base is below the main taxpayer's. A pure investor with no Spanish job or directorship does not qualify.

capital_gains.summary: Foreign capital gains are not taxed in Spain during the regime; gains on Spanish assets are taxed at 19% to 30%.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Spanish-source savings income scale 19%/21%/23%/27%/30% (30% above EUR 300,000; art. 93.2.e).2º LIRPF as amended by DF 7.3 Ley 7/2024, effective 1 January 2025).
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Employment income is taxed worldwide. Top rate on Spanish-source savings income: the BOE consolidated text of art. 93.2.e).2º LIRPF shows the scale 19% (to EUR 6,000), 21% (to 50,000), 23% (to 200,000), 27% (to 300,000) and 30% above, as amended by disposición final 7.3 of Ley 7/2024 (BOE-A-2024-26694) with effect from 1 January 2025; PwC's page (reviewed June 2026) still shows the pre-2025 28%, which is out of date. After the regime ends, the person is a normal resident; exit tax counts years of residence including the regime years.

capital_gains.rate_basis: Spanish-source gains: top of the art. 93 savings scale (30%). Foreign-source gains: outside the regime's taxable base (non-resident rules). private_business_sale assumes a Spanish company.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Foreign assets are outside the IRPF base during the regime; Modelo 720 reporting does not apply to regime taxpayers.

dividends.summary: Foreign dividends are not taxed in Spain during the regime; Spanish dividends are taxed at 19% to 30%.

dividends.rate_basis: Art. 93.2 LIRPF: only Spanish-source income is taxed; savings income at 19-30% (30% top since 1 January 2025, DF 7.3 Ley 7/2024, per the BOE consolidated text).
dividends.withholding_outbound: 19% domestic WHT on dividends to non-residents (corporate rule, unchanged).
dividends.treaty_network: A regime taxpayer is Spanish resident for IRPF but treaty access is often denied by source countries because the person is taxed only on Spanish income; expect full foreign WHT on the portfolio.

wealth_tax.summary: Wealth tax applies only to assets located in Spain (real obligation): 0.2% to 3.5% above EUR 700,000, plus the ITSGF where Spanish assets exceed about EUR 3.7m.
wealth_tax.exemptions_thresholds: EUR 700,000 allowance (art. 28.Tres LIP); the main-home exemption is debated for real-obligation taxpayers.
wealth_tax.important_exceptions: Foreign portfolio and foreign property are outside the base. Spanish real estate is taxed; regional rebates may apply depending on the region of the assets.

residency.tax_residency_test: Resident if more than 183 days in Spain in the calendar year (sporadic absences count unless foreign residence is proven), or if the main centre of economic interests is in Spain; rebuttable presumption if the non-separated spouse and minor children live in Spain. Nationals who move to a listed tax haven stay resident for that year and 4 more. The region of residence is the one where most days are spent (art. 28 Ley 22/2009).

routes.name: EU/EEA free movement
routes.requirements: Registration certificate (certificado de registro) after 3 months; proof of sufficient resources and health cover if not working.

routes.name: Non-lucrative residence visa
routes.requirements: Sufficient passive means and private health insurance; no work in Spain. Renewable, leads to long-term residence after 5 years.

routes.name: Highly qualified professional / international teleworker / entrepreneur permits (Ley 14/2013)
routes.requirements: Job offer, remote work for a foreign employer, or an approved business plan; these routes also open the Beckham regime.

routes.name: Golden visa (investor residence) - abolished
routes.requirements: Art. 63 Ley 14/2013 (investor visa) was left without content from 3 April 2025 by Ley Orgánica 1/2025; no new applications.

corporate.summary: CIT 25% (SMEs 23% in 2026, falling to 20% by 2029; start-ups 15%). Qualifying dividends and gains from stakes of at least 5% held 1 year are 95% exempt (participation exemption, art. 21 LIS - not re-verified for this file). Domestic WHT on outbound dividends 19%, 0% to EU parents. A holding company does not shelter a family's portfolio from the 30% personal savings rate on distribution.
corporate.special_zones: Canary Islands ZEC (4% CIT for qualifying substance), ETVE holding regime; SICAV 1% regime requires at least 100 investors with minimum stakes (since 2022).

us_citizen_notes: US citizens remain US-taxed. The Spain-US treaty has a saving clause; Spain gives a credit for US tax on US-source income within treaty limits. The Beckham regime removes Spanish tax on foreign investment income, so US tax becomes the only layer on it. Spanish wealth tax is not creditable in the US; Spanish inheritance tax paid by heirs may be creditable against US estate tax only in limited cases (no estate tax treaty with Spain).
open_questions: ITSGF has no end date; a reform of regional financing could replace it.
For newly arrived families, regional inheritance benefits depend on the deceased having spent most days of the prior 5 years in that region (art. 28 Ley 22/2009); days abroad count for no region.
Participation exemption details (art. 21 LIS) were not re-verified in this pass.
